title: This crate had way more polygons than it needed
author: Other-Light-6384
selftext:
A sci-fi storage crate shouldn't be the thing slowing down a game scene, but here we are.

The model came out of Meshy looking pretty decent. Nice panel details, solid overall shape, nothing obviously wrong. Then I opened it in Blender and checked the wireframe. Even the flat surfaces were covered in tiny triangles.

Blender's Decimate modifier seemed like the obvious fix. It brought the face count down, but the bevels started looking rough and some of the raised details barely survived. Not exactly the tradeoff I wanted.

Went back to Meshy and gave Remesh a shot, first with Fixed and then Adaptive at roughly the same target polycount. The difference was more noticeable than I expected. Similar numbers, but one version held the silhouette better while the other kept more of the small details.

The topology choice mattered too. Quads were easier to work with when adjusting parts of the crate in Blender, while triangles made sense for the version I wasn't planning to edit much further.

There was still some cleanup to do afterward. A few awkward faces, normals to check, the usual stuff. But at least I wasn't spending the whole time fighting the original dense mesh.

Kind of annoying how much work can hide behind a model that looks finished in the preview.

For game props like this, do you usually bother with automatic remeshing, or just manually retopo the areas that need work?
